解決真實嘅打包挑戰，使用 PyInstaller 同 Cython 將一個簡單嘅腳本轉變為單文件可執行程式，以實現性能優化同代碼保護。

Description:

Proposal title: AI-Powered Software Testing with Multi-Agent Systems
Abstract:
Traditional software testing struggles to keep pace with rapidly evolving applications—resulting in brittle test cases, time-consuming maintenance, and poor bug detection. This session introduces a smarter, adaptive approach using AI-powered Multi-Agent Systems that automate and continuously improve testing workflows.

We’ll explore how Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) transforms testing by dynamically generating test cases, adjusting to app changes in real-time, and detecting bugs with greater accuracy. Each agent has a specialized role—retrieving context, generating tests, and analyzing results—working together as a self-learning testing team.

The session will include a live walkthrough of a Python-based pipeline using PyTest, Selenium, LangChain, and ML models to:
• Automate UI and regression testing with minimal manual intervention
• Generate intelligent, context-aware test cases from code and API specs
• Use anomaly detection to flag subtle bugs based on test logs
• Continuously evolve test logic as the app evolves

By leveraging AI agents, teams can reduce manual QA efforts, improve test coverage, and increase reliability across fast-moving software projects. Whether you're a QA engineer, developer, or test automation architect, this talk will give you practical tools and ideas to build scalable, AI-driven QA systems using Python.
Description:
Dive into the future of software testing with AI-driven QA systems using Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). This session will demonstrate how to design and implement multi-agent systems that collaborate to automate UI testing, identify bugs, and adapt dynamically to application updates.

We’ll explore step-by-step methods for:

1)Integrating RAG techniques to retrieve and utilize relevant data for adaptive testing.
2)Building Python-based pipelines using libraries like PyTest, Selenium, and LangChain for seamless automation.
3)Automating bug detection with enhanced accuracy using machine learning models.
4)Optimizing test coverage with agents that learn and adapt to application changes.

This presentation is perfect for Python developers, QA testers, and engineers seeking practical approaches to enhance their testing workflows, reduce manual intervention, and ensure robust application performance in evolving software environments.
Notes:
Past Speaking Experience:
​
PyCon APAC Philippines 2025  and PyCon US Pittsburgh 2025 in May 2025.
​
I am active in tech communities and regularly contribute to open-source projects and forums on AI-driven testing.
​
Community Contributions:
​

​
Mentor & Advocate: Guide junior developers and QA engineers in adopting AI-powered testing practices.
​
This talk will provide practical, real-world insights into AI-driven testing with clear examples and actionable takeaways, making it valuable for developers, QA engineers, and automation testers.
What motivates you to submit this propos: As someone deeply involved in the Python community, I’m passionate about sharing practical, real-world applications of Python that solve meaningful problems. This proposal stems from my hands-on experience with Python in automation and AI-based QA testing. I’ve seen firsthand how intelligent systems can significantly reduce testing time and improve product quality. My motivation is to empower other developers and QA engineers by introducing them to these techniques, showing how they can apply Python beyond traditional scripting into smarter, scalable systems.
Why is this topic important for the Pyth: As AI and automation continue to evolve, the Python community stands at the forefront of building accessible, intelligent systems. This topic bridges two powerful areas AI and testing using Python’s rich ecosystem. It enables developers, testers, and even product teams to go beyond manual or rule-based testing and embrace smart, adaptive automation. By introducing multi-agent systems and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in QA, we push Python’s use into more innovative spaces, encouraging the community to adopt modern, efficient, and intelligent practices in software development.
What value will the audience gain?: Attendees will walk away with a practical understanding of how to build smarter, AI-powered test automation systems using Python. They’ll learn how to implement multi-agent workflows, integrate tools like PyTest, Selenium, and LangChain, and design scalable QA strategies powered by LLMs. The session will not only offer code-level insights but also real-world applications, challenges, and best practices helping engineers future-proof their testing skills and drive innovation in their teams.

Proposal title: GraphRAG with Python and Neo4j
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle to provide current and comprehensive answers from vast, interconnected knowledge bases, a common challenge in fields like business, legal and administrative tasks. While traditional RAG improves LLM context, it can falter with complex, relationship-heavy information. GraphRAG offers a powerful solution by leveraging graph databases to enhance retrieval with structured relationships, leading to deeper contextual understanding.

This talk provides a practical introduction to implementing GraphRAG using Neo4j. We will explore how Neo4j can be used to construct knowledge graphs from unstructured data and enable advanced, relationship-aware retrieval. Attendees will learn the core concepts of GraphRAG and gain practical insights to build smarter RAG systems, capable of delivering more accurate and contextually rich LLM responses for complex real-world applications.

GitHub Repo: https://github.com/hksquinson/pycon-hk-graphrag
Description:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized access to information, yet their inherent reliance on static training data often limits their ability to provide the most current, comprehensive, and contextually nuanced answers. This limitation is particularly evident when interacting with the vast, dynamically evolving, and highly interconnected knowledge bases found in many professional domains. 

While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) offers a significant step forward by allowing LLMs to access external information, it frequently struggles with the intricate relationships embedded within complex datasets. This challenge is acutely felt in sectors such as legal research, business intelligence, and corporate knowledge management, where the ability to precisely navigate extensive documents and extract deep, interconnected insights is critical for informed decision-making. Traditional RAG, in these scenarios, often fails to select truly relevant context, resulting in fragmented or incomplete answers.

GraphRAG directly addresses these limitations by recognizing that information often derives its true meaning from its connections. This powerful paradigm enhances RAG by leveraging the structural richness of graph databases to represent knowledge as a network of entities and their relationships. By doing so, GraphRAG empowers LLMs to not just retrieve isolated text snippets, but to intelligently traverse and query the underlying relationships, leading to a far more comprehensive and contextual understanding of information.

Attendees will discover:

* The fundamental principles of GraphRAG and its significant advantages over conventional RAG methods in handling complex, interconnected datasets—a critical capability for applications in business analysis, legal document interpretation, and comprehensive knowledge base exploration.
* How Neo4j efficiently structures and queries interconnected data, enabling optimal information retrieval.
* An overview of Python tools related to GraphRAG, showcasing its user-friendliness in building GraphRAG applications. This includes its capabilities for automated knowledge graph construction, extracting entities and relationships, and its support for various LLM providers and embedding models.
* Practical patterns for ingesting diverse data into Neo4j and leveraging its graph intelligence to enrich LLM prompts, thereby significantly improving the relevance, coherence, and depth of generated responses.

Whether you're a Python developer eager to build more sophisticated LLM applications, a data scientist exploring advanced retrieval techniques, or a professional in business, law or administration, this session will equip you with the foundational knowledge and practical insights to begin your journey with Neo4j-powered GraphRAG in a Python environment.
Notes:
While Neo4j is fundamentally a Java-based database, GraphRAG and its accompanying tools offer compelling reasons for a Python-focused discussion, specifically in two ways:

* Pythonic Approach: It's important to clarify that while Neo4j itself is a database written in Java, there are connections to Neo4j implemented in Python. It is possible for all GraphRAG development steps, from data ingestion to retrieval logic and integration with LLMs, to be done seamlessly within the Python ecosystem.

* Leveraging Python's AI Ecosystem: Developing GraphRAG in Python offers a significant advantage: seamless integration with the vast array of AI and data science libraries. This includes popular tools like Hugging Face's `transformers` for advanced natural language processing (e.g., entity extraction, summarization), `pandas` for efficient data manipulation and analysis, and other machine learning frameworks. This powerful synergy allows for highly flexible and customizable GraphRAG workflows.
What motivates you to submit this propos: Drawing from my experience building a GraphRAG system for my undergraduate final year project, I am motivated to share the practical potential of this cutting-edge approach, making it accessible to the broader Python community and inspiring its adoption for real-world challenges.
Why is this topic important for the Pyth: This talk highlights how the Python ecosystem, empowers developers to build sophisticated GraphRAG applications, addressing critical limitations of traditional LLMs with interconnected data, and fostering innovation within Python's AI landscape.
What value will the audience gain?: Attendees will gain foundational knowledge of GraphRAG and practical insights into leveraging Neo4j in Python, enabling them to build more accurate, contextual, and robust LLM-powered solutions for complex data problems in their own projects and organizations.

Proposal title: AI in Open Source Project Management: More than Just Code
Abstract: Open source isn’t just about code—it’s about people, coordination, and community. As projects grow, non-code responsibilities like triaging, onboarding, and communication can become overwhelming. In this talk, we’ll explore how AI tools can support open-source project management by automating routine tasks, improving decision-making, and boosting contributor experience. You’ll discover practical, lesser-known tools and learn how to integrate AI responsibly into your project workflows
Description:
Open-source projects often rely on the passion of contributors, but behind every successful release is a mountain of non-code effort like managing issues, onboarding contributors, planning releases, and keeping the community engaged. As projects scale, these tasks can become difficult to manage manually.
This session introduces a practical way forward using AI.We’ll explore real use cases where AI can enhance open-source workflows, such as:
Intelligent issue triaging and classification
Contributor behavior insights (e.g., burnout signals, activity patterns)
NLP-powered summarization of long discussions
Auto-generation of documentation, changelogs, and onboarding materials
l will also introduce  useful and often overlooked tools like Codex Automator, Issue Label Bot, Sourcery, Remotion.dev, Athenian, and LinearB. These tools help teams automate, analyze, and communicate better, without replacing the human connections that drive open-source communities.
We’ll also examine ethical considerations such as data privacy and algorithmic bias, and walk through a real-world example from a Python community initiative that piloted AI-driven onboarding.
By the end of this session, the audience will walk away with actionable strategies, tools to explore, and a new outlook on managing open-source projects smarter, not harder
What motivates you to submit this propos:
As a Service Delivery Manager and lead in the Python community, I’ve learned that the biggest bottlenecks in open-source projects are rarely technical, they’re about coordination, clarity, and contributor experience. In my role as Communications Lead for PyLadies Ghana, I’ve helped organize workshops, manage global partnerships, and onboard new contributors. These experiences exposed me to the growing complexity of running community-driven projects, and the invisible workload that comes with it.
This talk was inspired by the real challenges I’ve faced managing people and processes across distributed teams. I’ve been exploring how AI tools can help automate repetitive tasks, streamline communication, and make our work more sustainable. By sharing practical use cases and tools, I hope to support other open-source leaders and contributors who are trying to scale their impact without burning out.
PyCon Hong Kong is a space that celebrates both technical depth and community connection, and I’m excited for the chance to contribute to that conversation.
Why is this topic important for the Pyth:
This topic is important to the Python community because open-source projects, especially in the Python ecosystem, thrive on collaboration, not just code. As the community continues to grow, so do the challenges of managing distributed teams, maintaining contributor engagement, and coordinating project workflows. These challenges often fall on a few dedicated maintainers and community leads, leading to burnout and reduced sustainability.

By exploring how AI can support project management, onboarding, and communication, this session addresses a critical but often overlooked aspect of community success. It introduces practical tools and strategies that can help Python projects scale more sustainably, reduce manual overhead, and create better experiences for both new and experienced contributors. In a language ecosystem known for accessibility and community spirit, it’s essential that we also focus on making the management side of open source just as inclusive, efficient, and forward-thinking.
What value will the audience gain?:
The audience will walk away with a practical understanding of how AI can be used to solve real-world challenges in open-source project management—beyond just writing code. They’ll gain insight into how to streamline issue triaging, improve contributor onboarding, monitor team health, and reduce manual workload using lesser-known AI tools.

Whether they’re project maintainers, community leads, or active contributors, attendees will leave with actionable strategies, tool recommendations, and ethical considerations they can apply to their own projects. This talk will empower them to lead smarter, scale sustainably, and build healthier, more collaborative Python communities

Proposal title: Beyond the GIL: Python Concurrency Essentials
Abstract:
Python’s Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) is often portrayed as a limitation but it doesn’t have to be a blocker.  In this talk, we will discuss the core concepts behind Python concurrency and explore practical ways to work with  GIL rather than working against it. From threading to multiprocessing, async IO to real-world patterns, we will break down what’s really going on under the hood and when to use which approach.

Whether you are building data pipelines, web backends, or automating workflows, understanding concurrency is key to writing responsive and efficient Python code. I will use simple examples and real life scenarios to show how concurrency works in modern Python and share some hard earned lessons from debugging slow, blocking code in production systems.
Description:
What the audience will learn:

What the GIL is and how it affects concurrency in Python

When to use threads, processes, or asyncio (and when not to)

Practical patterns for real-world Python projects

How to think about performance and responsiveness beyond "faster code"

Proposal title: From MongoDB to Postgres: Building an Open Source Standard for Document Databases
Abstract:
MongoDB has become a widely adopted database across industries due to its ease of use, but its shift away from open source and licensing challenges have raised concerns. Running MongoDB also demands additional resources and expertise. Is there a viable alternative? Can we seamlessly migrate MongoDB workloads to Postgres without making application-level changes? And how can MongoDB users continue using their familiar tools and frameworks?
In this talk, we will explore the current state of document databases and the growing need for a new open-source standard. We propose that Postgres should be the backbone for this new standard, offering a robust, flexible, and open alternative. By integrating FerretDB, we'll show how Postgres can handle MongoDB workloads with ease. We’ll also demonstrate how to leverage MongoDB tools to manage your Postgres database as if it were MongoDB.
This approach bridges the gap between Postgres and the MongoDB community, bringing new possibilities for both users and developers while contributing to Postgres's ongoing success.

Proposal title: What's new in pandas 3.0
Abstract: pandas 3.0 is going to be released in the next months. While pandas hasn't changed much since it became popular many years ago, pandas 3 does bring some interesting new features that will make working with data easier, faster and more powerful. In this talk I will explain what's new in pandas 3.0.

Proposal title: Pyodide: Python Reborn in the Browser
Abstract:
Have you ever wished you could run Python directly in the browser—without any server backend or WebSocket setup?

In this talk, I will introduce Pyodide, a WebAssembly-based Python distribution that brings the full Python runtime to the browser. You’ll learn how Pyodide enables scientific computing, data visualization, and interactive notebooks—all in client-side web apps. We’ll explore how Pyodide is built, how to integrate it with JavaScript, and the real-world limitations to watch out for.

Whether you're building a no-backend playground, an AI-enabled tool, or an offline-capable app, Pyodide opens new doors for Python in the frontend.
Description:
Pyodide is an emerging solution for running Python in the browser using WebAssembly. In this session, I will:

1. Explain the architecture and use cases of Pyodide.
2. Show how to build apps that combine Pyodide with modern web frameworks (e.g., React, Vue).
3. Demo real-world use cases including AI model inference, scientific visualization, and interactive education tools.
4. Discuss Pyodide's ecosystem, performance tips, and current limitations.

This talk is suitable for Python developers curious about frontend technologies, WebAssembly enthusiasts, and anyone exploring the boundaries of full-stack Python.
Notes: The speaker has implemented several real-world projects using Pyodide. Source code and live demos will be provided.
What motivates you to submit this propos: As a Python educator, I’ve always sought tools that reduce barriers to learning. Pyodide has empowered me to teach scientific computing—like numpy, pandas, and scipy—directly in the browser without any local setup. Submitting this talk is my way of sharing how educators and developers alike can build frictionless, interactive learning tools using Pyodide.
Why is this topic important for the Pyth: Pyodide makes Python education truly accessible. Many students and beginners struggle with package installations and environment issues. With Pyodide, Python (including data science libraries) can be used directly in the browser—no setup, no dependencies. This is crucial for democratizing Python and making scientific computing more inclusive and scalable.
What value will the audience gain?:
Attendees will learn:
- How Pyodide works and how to load popular scientific libraries.
- How to build browser-based Python notebooks or teaching demos.
- How to embed Python in web apps for education or experimentation.
- Best practices and limitations from real teaching use cases.

Proposal title: My Poor Fund: How MPF Fees Are Eating Your Retirement
Abstract: Hong Kong’s Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) is supposed to secure your retirement—but what if it’s secretly shrinking your savings? Using Python, we’ll simulate how high fees erode your returns over time, compare MPF performance against low-cost alternatives (like index funds), and uncover whether sticking with the default plan could cost you millions. Through interactive visualisations, we’ll expose the maths behind, and explore how self-directed investing might be the escape hatch.

Proposal title: Building DSLs in Python using YACC
Abstract:
In today's rapidly evolving technological landscape, the demand for software solutions is more critical than ever. General-purpose programming languages, while versatile, often fall short in addressing the specific needs of various domains. DSLs have been gaining significant traction in recent years due to their ability to provide elegant abstractions tailored to specific domains. This presentation outlines the importance of creating Domain-Specific Languages (DSLs) and how they can enhance productivity, improve communication, and optimize performance in specialized fields.

The YACC (Yet Another Compiler Compiler) library in Python offers a powerful framework for building these DSLs, enabling developers to create languages that are both expressive and efficient. YACC is a tool used to generate parsers for context-free grammars, allowing the creation of interpreters and compilers for DSLs. In Python, libraries such as PLY (Python Lex-Yacc) implement YACC-like functionality, enabling developers to define grammars and parse input effectively. In particular, this presentation will demonstrate the capabilities of Python's powerful YACC library in the development of DSLs. We will also share our insights and experiences in utilizing Python to create a network programming language.
What motivates you to submit this propos: DSLs are becoming increasingly important in modern programming paradigms. It is essential to understand the role of powerful tools provided in Python ecosystem for building DSLs.
What value will the audience gain?: The audience will get to know the DSL building libraries provided in Python. Audience will also benefit from the real use case of using YACC in building a network programming language at industry scale.

Proposal title: Vibe Testing with Playwright and AI
Abstract:
In today's fast-paced development landscape, simply verifying that features work is no longer enough. Users expect intuitive, engaging, and seamless digital experiences – a certain "vibe." This talk introduces the emerging concept of "vibe testing," an approach to quality assurance that focuses on assessing the intangible aspects of user experience, emotional engagement, and overall fluidity, moving beyond traditional functional checks.

We'll explore how Artificial Intelligence, specifically Large Language Models and Vision-Language Models, can revolutionize this subjective domain. Learn how to leverage Playwright, the robust browser automation framework, as the foundation for building intelligent agents. We'll dive into the Playwright Model Context Protocol, a powerful tool that enables LLMs to interact with web pages through structured accessibility snapshots, offering a more efficient and reliable alternative to pixel-based automation for AI. We'll demonstrate how these AI agents can simulate human-like exploration, interpret user sentiment, and uncover subtle usability issues, enhancing the qualitative aspects of your testing.
Description:
This presentation will explore a crucial evolution in software quality assurance: the shift from purely functional testing to evaluating the holistic user experience. We will introduce "vibe testing," a contemporary approach focused on assessing the intangible aspects of an application, such as its intuitiveness, emotional engagement, and overall user satisfaction. The aim is to ensure that software not only performs its intended functions but also delivers a truly positive and impactful user experience.

We will demonstrate how Artificial Intelligence, particularly Large Language Models and Vision-Language Models, can significantly enhance and scale this qualitative evaluation. The talk will highlight Playwright as the robust browser automation framework serving as the foundation for building intelligent AI agents capable of sophisticated web interactions. A key component of our discussion will be the Playwright Model Context Protocol, explaining how this innovative protocol enables LLMs to interpret and interact with web pages using structured accessibility information, thereby overcoming the limitations often associated with pixel-based automation.

Through practical examples and conceptual insights, we will illustrate how these AI agents can simulate human-like exploration patterns, identify subtle UI/UX inconsistencies, and even infer user sentiment or potential frustration by analyzing interaction flows. This session is designed to equip Python developers, QA engineers, and those interested in cutting-edge testing methodologies with the knowledge and tools to integrate advanced AI capabilities into their Playwright-based testing strategies. By the conclusion of this talk, attendees will understand how to move beyond conventional testing to effectively capture and enhance the "vibe" of their web applications.
What motivates you to submit this propos: My motivation stems from the exciting potential of combining Playwright with AI to enhance software quality beyond traditional functional testing. I believe "vibe testing" represents a crucial next step in user experience, and I'm eager to share practical approaches and tools like Playwright MCP with the PyCon HK community.
Why is this topic important for the Pyth: This topic is crucial because it merges Python's strength in AI with Playwright's automation power to tackle sophisticated UX challenges. It enables Python developers to build innovative "vibe testing" solutions, elevating software quality and keeping the community at the forefront of AI-driven testing trends.
What value will the audience gain?: Attendees will learn to integrate Playwright with AI (specifically Playwright MCP) for advanced "vibe testing," enabling them to create more intelligent, user-centric automated tests and stay ahead in AI-driven QA.

Proposal title: From Paperwork to Python: Building a Document Automation System
Abstract:
Repetitive, document-driven tasks — such as reports, audits, and questionnaires — are a time-consuming burden across industries. In this lightning talk about a personal project, I will share how I built a Python-based system to automate such workflows using natural language understanding and information retrieval techniques. Using a combination of pytesseract for optical character recognition (OCR), document question-answering, Top-N filtering, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the system generates accurate, context-aware responses from unstructured documents.

I will also share strategies for preparing and refining datasets to support domain-specific automation. Whether you are preparing contracts, completing due-diligence questionnaires, or handling customer intake forms, this talk will offer a practical blueprint for transforming tedious workflows into scalable systems.
Description: A lightning talk on how Python and NLP can transform document-heavy workflows into scalable systems.
What motivates you to submit this propos:
This project grew out of a Google hackathon where I have received an honorable mention, a recognition that meant a lot to me as it validated an idea that I was deeply passionate about — document automation. 

Having worked in tax technology consulting before, I saw firsthand how document-heavy workflows led to costly errors and delays in important filings. I was motivated to use Python to reduce that friction through automation, and share what I have learnt in the PyCon community.
Why is this topic important for the Pyth: The PyCon community is incredibly diverse, with members coming from nearly every industry — most of which face document-heavy workflows in some form. This lightning talk aims to offer a reusable blueprint and a practical strategy to help overcome those challenges.
What value will the audience gain?:
Attendees will gain:
1. A reusable framework for document automation through pytesseract, document question-answering models, and retrieval-augmented generation
2. Strategies to design effective domain-specific datasets

Proposal title: 一個由 Python 支援嘅 LLM Code Generation 嘅 Benchmark
Abstract:
喺現今人工智能驅動嘅世界入面，唔少 LLM 都自稱係coding冠軍，但係我哋點樣超越簡單嘅「hello, world」提示，嚴格同可重複噉測試佢哋嘅真正code generate能力？
呢個講座介紹一個全面嘅基準測試套件，完全係用 Python 構建，旨在回答呢個問題。我哋用咗經典嘅掃雷遊戲作為一個唔簡單嘅標準化挑戰。
我哋會示範呢個工具可以點樣透過靈活嘅 API 比較唔同嘅模型（由 GPT-4 到local LLM），發掘一個強大嘅開源方法去評估 LLM
Description:
Part 1: The Problem - Why Benchmarking LLMs is Hard (5 mins)
The challenge of evaluating generative code: it's non-deterministic and context-dependent.
Why simple prompts are insufficient for measuring true capability.
Introducing our solution: Using Minesweeper as a standardized, complex, and fun benchmark task.
A quick overview of our multi-faceted scoring system (success, partial success, time, etc.).
Part 2: The Tool in Action - Live Demonstration (10 mins)
Standalone Mode: Running the script directly from the command line to test a local Python solver. We'll show the console output and generated result files.
Server Mode:
Starting the Flask-based web service.
Using curl to submit a benchmark job for a real LLM (e.g., GPT-4) with a custom prompt via our REST API.
Polling the /status endpoint to check progress.
Retrieving the final, structured JSON summary from the /result endpoint.
Part 3: The Engineering Journey - A Python Deep-Dive (10 mins)
From a single script to a concurrent powerhouse using concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor.
The "Wall of Errors": A candid walkthrough of the real-world challenges we faced and solved:
The use_reloader=False fix: How dynamic script creation breaks Flask's development server.
The multiprocessing.Manager fix: Solving the classic "shared state" problem across spawned processes on Windows.
The if __name__ == '__main__': safeguard: Why it's absolutely critical for multiprocessing.
The explicit parameter passing fix: Why relying on a global app context in child processes is a trap.
This section is designed to be highly educational, sharing hard-won lessons in robust Python application design.
Part 4: Conclusion & Takeaways (5 mins)
Recap of the tool's capabilities and architecture.
Key takeaways for the audience: How to apply these patterns to their own projects, and a call to action to use or contribute to the tool.
Q&A.

What the audience will learn:
A novel and effective method for benchmarking LLM code generation.
How to structure a Python project that can function both as a standalone CLI tool and a modular web service component.
Practical, real-world solutions to common and tricky problems in Python's multiprocessing.
Best practices for designing a simple, stateful API service with background tasks using Flask.
They will leave with access to an open-source tool they can use immediately for their own LLM evaluations.

Proposal title: Open Standards and Open Source: An Introduction
Abstract: Delve into the world of Open Source and Open Standards in this informative talk. We'll define Open Source, explore its licenses, and showcase software examples, followed by the workings of Open Source projects. We'll then shift to Open Standards, offering definitions, examples, and insights into their creation. The discussion includes a comparison of values between Open Source and Open Standards, the evolution of SQL as an Open Standard, its relationship with Open Source, and historical parallels in Document Databases. Peter's personal connection to the subject adds a unique perspective to this comprehensive introduction.

Proposal title: Memory Efficient Iteration with Python's itertools- A Deep Dive
Abstract: In today’s data-driven world, handling large datasets efficiently is crucial for any developer or data scientist. Python's itertools module offers a suite of fast and memory efficient tools to handle extensive data iteration, making it a great solution for managing large datasets without exhausting system resources. This talk will dive into several key functions of itertools comparing them to native Python iterations. Attendees will learn how to streamline their code and reduce memory usage while maintaining high performance.
Description:
While itertools is part of Python’s standard library, it is often overlooked by many developers in favor of more familiar, but less efficient, native methods. This talk will emphasize the importance of understanding and using these memory-efficient tools, particularly when working with large datasets, where performance and resource management are critical. We’ll begin with a discussion of common challenges developers face when handling large-scale data and why default iteration methods can lead to memory exhaustion or slow performance.

Next, we’ll explore key itertools functions like chain, islice, and cycle, demonstrating how they can drastically reduce memory usage while maintaining high speed. More advanced tools like groupby, product, and permutations will also be covered, showing their relevance in complex data processing scenarios. Real-world examples and benchmarks will clearly illustrate how itertools outperforms native Python approaches in both memory efficiency and speed.

By the end of this session, attendees will not only understand how to incorporate itertools into their workflows but will also gain actionable strategies to write more efficient and optimized Python code. This knowledge will empower them to tackle large datasets with confidence, leading to faster, more scalable applications in data science, software development, and beyond.

Talk Outline:
Overview of iteration challenges and importance of memory-efficient iteration(5 minutes)
Introduction to itertools (5 minutes)

Proposal title: Building Consistent & Secure Container Environments
Abstract:
*"It works on my machine"* is the developer equivalent of *"the dog ate my homework"*—and we've all been there.

Picture this: Your dev environment is a beautiful snowflake. So is your teammate's. And production? That's a whole different animal. Now imagine if they were all... the same. Not just similar. Actually identical.

But here's the kicker: what if that identical environment was also actually secure? Not "we ran a scanner once" secure, but "built from the ground up with security baked in" secure. Zero known vulnerabilities instead of the usual 200+, complete software bill of materials included.

This talk is about ditching the chaos and building environments that are consistent, secure by default, and work the same whether you're coding at 2am or deploying to production.

We'll explore Dev Containers and Wolfi—practical patterns that'll make your life easier, your deployments more reliable, and your security team actually happy for once.

Proposal title: Unscripted Yes, Consistent Commitment: From Meetup Attendee to PyCon APAC 2025 Co-Chair Journey
Abstract:
Many hesitate to join tech communities or take on leadership roles, fearing they’re not "ready." My journey was anything but planned—I simply said "yes" to opportunities, even when unprepared. From attending meetups as a newcomer to becoming a core volunteer and now PyCon APAC 2025 Co-Chair, my story is one of commitment, uncertainty, and growth.

In this talk, I’ll share how showing up, embracing challenges, and volunteering transformed my career and community involvement. I'll also break down common misconceptions about tech meetups and how anyone regardless of experience can start contributing. If you’re hesitant to take that first step, this talk will inspire you to leap, learn, and find your place in the Python and tech community.
Description:
Many believe that to contribute meaningfully to a tech community, they need to be an expert or have years of experience. But my journey proves otherwise. I started as someone who simply showed up attending meetups, learning from others, and saying "yes" to volunteering, even when I wasn’t sure what I was getting into. What followed was an unexpected but transformative journey, from a local Python volunteer to co-chairing PyCon APAC 2025.

In this talk, I’ll share how my "fake it till you make it" mindset and consistent commitment led me to this point. I'll discuss how I navigated the world of Python & tech meetups, the lessons I learned from being a tech community nomad, and the surprising impact of small actions in community growth. Attendees will gain insights into how they can start their own journey, overcome self-doubt, and make meaningful contributions, no matter their skill level.

By the end of this talk, I hope to inspire more people to step up, take a leap of faith, and actively engage in the Python and tech community because every great journey starts with a simple "yes."
Notes:
As someone coming from the absolute nothingness knowledge of pursuing this course. My basic go to is youtube, and joining fb groups as i perceived them "more realistic" information like true to life sharings. That's where i stumbled on webinars and my favorite part is Q&A as i can go freely ask them what i want. That consistent of seeking answers and finding out new things leads me to attending MANY meetups(even my family scoleded me for it because it is always night time and i am from far away from the business districts where meetup always happen) and volunteering.

I joined stagehand committee and got accepted eventhough what i only know is sharing through full-screen window, no OBS, no other softwares. i became lead for the swags committee too, managing printables and items. Not knowing there will be process of quotation test prints, and i don't even know what is GSM(paper thickness), and difference between matte and glossy.

Up until now being a PyCon APAC 2025 Co-Chair, trying uncharted waters again. but through commitment and activeness to complete it. i was able to accomplish it. thanks too from the help of my mentors and fellow volunteers.
What motivates you to submit this propos: As someone that gain what I have right now through tech communities especially Python Philippines that hones me. I advocate for attending tech meetups and strive to bridge the gap between society and tech communities. Many people are held back by misconceptions and systemic barriers, and I believe it's essential to create inclusive, welcoming spaces that encourage broader participation, hopefully by sharing my journey(that consists of a lot of leap of faith!) and what i know, i do hope i'm able to make them inspire and maybe take engagement to tech communities(maybe volunteering too)
Why is this topic important for the Pyth: It showcases my ground zero journey to become PyCon APAC 2025 Co-Chair. It emphasize the importance of taking risk and being consistent with it to accomplish your goal.
What value will the audience gain?:
Target Audience:

- Newcomers to tech communities who feel hesitant about joining or contributing.
- Aspiring volunteers looking to get more involved in Python or local tech communities.
- Community organizers interested in fostering more inclusive participation.


Key Takeaways:

- Breaking misconceptions about attending meetups(you need to be expert, emphasizing meetups is for new comers too, etc.) and volunteering.
- The importance of consistency, engagement, and stepping outside your comfort zone.
- How small actions can lead to unexpected growth and leadership opportunities.

Proposal title: Lessons Learned from Launching KangaCode: An EdTech Startup with Python from MVP to International Impact
Abstract:
What if you could turn a small python project into an internationally recognized EdTech platform?

This talk shares the real-world journey of building KangaCode, a game-based learning platform that teaches Python to K–12 students. Learn how we moved from a scrappy MVP to a startup supported by Carnegie Mellon University—powered entirely by Python. You’ll hear about the architecture, the challenges, and the strategies that helped us scale across borders and classrooms. Perfect for developers, educators, and anyone curious about Python in action beyond traditional software.
Description:
In this talk, I’ll walk through how we built KangaCode, a game-based platform that helps K–12 students write their first line of Python through interactive storytelling and real-time feedback. What started as a small MVP developed with Django and Pygame has grown into an international learning tool supported by Carnegie Mellon University.

We’ll explore:

1. How we used Django and Pygame to create a working MVP in under 3 months
2. Why Python was the ideal choice for educational games and fast iteration
3. Building a real-time code sandbox with safety and feedback mechanisms
4. Technical and operational challenges we encountered while scaling globally
5. Lessons from working with schools and educators across different cultures

This talk is ideal for developers interested in building Python-powered platforms, especially in education, social impact, or early-stage startups. Whether you're building for fun or aiming for product-market fit, you'll walk away with ideas, architecture tips, and insights to accelerate your own projects.
Notes:
I am the Co-Founder and Developer Lead at Roulettech, Inc., where I lead the development of KangaCode — a gamified learning platform designed to teach Python through interactive gameplay and real-time feedback. KangaCode is currently supported by Carnegie Mellon University, the Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship, where we receive mentorship and entrepreneurial support.

I hold a master's degree from the University of Pittsburgh and have taught Python programming to groups of 8–18 year-olds in both English and Mandarin, often in workshop and classroom settings with 5–15 students. I have years of experience in Python development, educational product design, and facilitating hands-on learning experiences for younger students.

While this will be my first time speaking at PyCon HK, I have delivered technical presentations and live coding demos in educational settings and community events. My work focuses on the intersection of software engineering, curriculum design, and playful learning. I’m passionate about helping beginners write their first line of code in a way that is engaging, safe, and immediately rewarding.

I look forward to sharing both the technical challenges and educational insights we encountered while building KangaCode, and hope to contribute a practical, experience-driven perspective to the Python education community.
What motivates you to submit this propos: As the Co-Founder and CEO of an EdTech startup supported by Carnegie Mellon University, I’ve experienced firsthand how Python can be the backbone of both rapid prototyping and long-term scalability. I’m motivated to share my journey—from building our first MVP with Django and Pygame, to scaling across users in Taiwan and the U.S.—to inspire other developers considering launching their own Python-powered ventures. PyCon Hong Kong is an ideal venue to connect with others passionate about applying Python beyond traditional development into impactful real-world solutions.
Why is this topic important for the Pyth: Many developers dream of turning their side projects into real-world products, but few talks demystify that path. By sharing concrete examples of how Python enabled both speed and stability for our startup—handling real-time code execution, data flow, user management, and education-specific needs—this talk offers a roadmap for how to move from hackathon project to production-grade EdTech platform. It also shows how the Python ecosystem enables not just technical development, but innovation in education and social impact.
What value will the audience gain?:
Attendees will walk away with:

1. A behind-the-scenes look at how to launch and grow a Python-based product
2. Insights into selecting the right Python stack (Django, Pygame, AWS Lambda, etc.) for rapid iteration and long-term growth
3. Lessons from scaling in international markets with limited resources
4. Tips on balancing product, pedagogy, and engineering in an EdTech context

Whether you’re an aspiring founder, Python enthusiast, or educator, this talk offers practical takeaways for anyone looking to turn Python projects into real products.

Proposal title: Grafana is the GOAT: Observability for FastAPI with the LGTM Stack
Abstract:
Your FastAPI app is fast — but what happens when it fails fast?

This talk will show you how to level up your production observability using the open-source LGTM stack: Loki (logs), Grafana (dashboards), Tempo (traces), and Mimir/Prometheus (metrics). Paired with OpenTelemetry, you’ll get real-time insight into what's happening in your Python app — no more flying blind in production.

Inspired by the Fireship “LGTM” video, this session is packed with practical, demo-driven content focused on Python, FastAPI, and Docker-friendly observability.
Description:
1. Cold Open (2 min)
We’ll kick things off with a hard truth:
“If builders built houses like we write code, the first woodpecker would end civilization.”
* Why observability is no longer optional:
    * Downtime kills trust
    * Bugs go unnoticed until it’s too late
* FastAPI is blazingly fast — but when it fails, it fails fast
* We need visibility, not just velocity

2. Meet the LGTM Stack (5 min)
Learn how the LGTM stack brings observability to your Python apps:
* Loki – for collecting and searching logs
* Grafana – for dashboards, alerts, and visualizations
* Tempo – for distributed tracing
* Prometheus/Mimir – for time-series metrics
Understand why logs + metrics + traces are the “Holy Trinity” of modern observability

3. Setting Up Your Stack (5 min)
We’ll walk through a simple, self-hosted setup:
* Use a single docker-compose file to run the entire LGTM stack
* Deploy it Fireship-style on an affordable VPS
* All open-source, easy to maintain, and no vendor lock-in

4. Instrumenting FastAPI with OpenTelemetry (8 min)
Bring observability into your FastAPI project using OpenTelemetry:
* Key libraries:
    * opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi
    * opentelemetry-exporter-otlp
* Send real-time telemetry to the LGTM stack
* Add custom instrumentation:
    * Metrics – track request latency, response counts, etc.
    * Traces – follow route execution and database calls
    * Logs – structured with context, levels, and correlation

5. Viewing Telemetry in Grafana (5 min)
See how to make sense of the data you’re collecting:
* RED metrics dashboards (Rate, Errors, Duration)
* Latency histograms from Prometheus
* Loki logs – search by route or status code
* Tempo traces – visualize the full lifecycle of requests
No more guessing where the error came from — see it

6. Bonus: Continuous Profiling (2 min)
Take it one step further with Pyroscope:
* Integrated profiling of CPU and memory usage
* Visualize performance hotspots with flame graphs
* Compare profiles between deploys

7. Wrap-Up & Takeaways (2–3 min)
* Full-stack observability — fully Pythonic
* Turn “it works on my machine” into “it works in prod”
* Everything covered is open-source, fast, and ready for real-world use
Notes:
Who’s it for?
Python devs using FastAPI, Flask, or Django

Anyone running self-hosted apps

Engineers tired of debugging production issues in the dark

No prior observability experience required — bring your code and curiosity.
What motivates you to submit this propos: I submitted this proposal because many Python developers build fast APIs with FastAPI but struggle when things inevitably fail in production. Observability often feels complex or out of reach. Inspired by the simple and catchy LGTM concept (Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir), I want to share a practical, hands-on approach to help Python devs gain clear, real-time insights into their apps without overwhelming complexity. This talk bridges the gap between fast development and reliable operations.
Why is this topic important for the Pyth: The LGTM stack paired with OpenTelemetry offers an open-source, Docker-friendly, and scalable observability solution tailored for Python ecosystems. Highlighting this stack helps the community move beyond guesswork and maintain high-quality services in production.
What value will the audience gain?:
Attendees will:

Understand how to implement a complete observability pipeline for FastAPI using the LGTM stack.

Learn how to integrate OpenTelemetry for rich telemetry data in Python apps.

See live demos of setting up Loki for logs, Grafana for dashboards, Tempo for tracing, and Mimir for metrics.

Gain practical skills to monitor, diagnose, and improve FastAPI apps running in Docker or Kubernetes.

Leave confident in their ability to prevent “failing fast” from becoming “failing blind.”

This talk empowers Python developers to turn fast code into reliable, observable services.

Proposal title: Observability for FastAPI: Building Continuously Reliable Services with Grafana OSS
Abstract:
FastAPI makes it fast to build APIs. But how do you ensure those APIs are continuously reliable in real-world environments?

In this talk, we’ll explore observability from a Python/DevOps perspective using Grafana’s open-source stack—including Loki (logs), Prometheus & Mimir (metrics), Tempo (traces), and Pyroscope (continuous profiling). You'll learn how to integrate OpenTelemetry with FastAPI, visualize your service behavior in Grafana, and catch performance regressions before they cause incidents.

Whether you're running FastAPI in containers, VMs, or serverless, this talk will give you the tools to observe, understand, and improve your backend services.
Description:
1. Why Observability Matters for FastAPI (5 mins)
Building systems isn't enough; they must survive reality

Continuous reliability as a goal

What FastAPI apps need: speed, safety, insights

2. The Four Pillars of Observability (10 mins)
Logs (Loki): Capturing structured FastAPI logs

Metrics (Prometheus/Mimir): Uptime, latency, error rates

Traces (Tempo): Following a request through dependencies

Profiles (Pyroscope): Finding CPU or memory bottlenecks

3. Instrumenting FastAPI with OpenTelemetry (10 mins)
Setup with opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi

Exporting data to Grafana stack

Hands-on code demo: add metrics, traces, logs

4. Collecting & Routing Telemetry (5 mins)
Grafana Alloy: the new unified telemetry collector

Working with OpenTelemetry Collector, Prometheus Agent

Containerized deployment tips for Alloy

5. Visualizing & Alerting with Grafana (5 mins)
Connecting data sources in Grafana

Dashboards for latency, throughput, errors (RED)

Alerting with Grafana + OnCall (Slack, PagerDuty, etc.)

6. Continuous Profiling with Pyroscope (5 mins)
Integration with Python apps using pyroscope-py

Viewing flame graphs, identifying hot spots

Comparing performance before/after deploys

7. Synthetic Testing with k6 (5 mins)
Generate load before going live

Simulate real FastAPI usage

Use test scripts to validate performance

8. Best Practices & Pitfalls (5 mins)
Avoiding alert fatigue

Keeping overhead low

Making observability part of CI/CD

🔧 Live Demo:
Real-time metrics & traces from a FastAPI app

Grafana dashboard and flame graph walkthrough
Notes:
Target Audience:
Python developers building APIs with FastAPI

DevOps/SREs responsible for system reliability

Teams adopting OpenTelemetry and Grafana

Engineers seeking practical tools for observability
What motivates you to submit this propos: FastAPI is now a go-to framework for modern Python APIs, but once these services are deployed, many teams struggle to observe, debug, and optimize them in production. I submitted this proposal because observability isn't optional anymore—it's the foundation of reliable systems. I've seen firsthand how tools like Prometheus, Loki, and Pyroscope can turn black-box Python services into fully transparent, tunable systems. This talk aims to make observability accessible for FastAPI developers who want to ship faster, safer, and smarter.
Why is this topic important for the Pyth: FastAPI is growing rapidly within the Python ecosystem, especially in production-grade systems and microservices. However, observability practices often lag behind development speed. This talk gives Python developers a practical framework—logs, metrics, traces, and profiling—applied specifically to FastAPI and powered by modern tools like OpenTelemetry and Grafana. It’s important because developers can’t fix what they can’t see, and this session will show them how to see everything without reinventing the wheel.
What value will the audience gain?:
Attendees will leave with:

A step-by-step understanding of how to add observability to FastAPI apps using real tools (Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope).

Working knowledge of instrumenting FastAPI with OpenTelemetry for logs, metrics, and traces.

Techniques to route telemetry using tools like Grafana Alloy and deploy observability setups in containerized environments.

Best practices for visualization and alerting using Grafana dashboards and OnCall.

Exposure to continuous profiling and synthetic testing to ensure performance doesn’t regress after each deployment.

They’ll walk out with actionable insights and code snippets to make their FastAPI apps production-ready and resilient—with confidence that they’ll know when something breaks, and why.
